docs.title: DevOps Challenge — Overview
docs.text:
A production-style FastAPI application running on AWS, built to demonstrate:

  • Containerised Python app with a clean REST API
  • Infrastructure-as-code with Terraform (modular)
  • Automated CI/CD with GitHub Actions (build → test → push → deploy)
  • Observability via CloudWatch

docs.text: Page What it covers Architecture AWS resources and how they connect Local Development Run the app on your machine with Docker Compose Deployment Step-by-step guide to provision and deploy Infrastructure Terraform modules and variables reference CI/CD Pipeline GitHub Actions jobs, secrets, and rollback API Reference All endpoints with request/response examples

docs.title: Tech stack
docs.text: Layer Technology Application Python 3.11 · FastAPI · Uvicorn Container Docker · Docker Compose Registry Amazon ECR Compute AWS EC2 t3.micro (Amazon Linux 2) Networking AWS VPC · Public subnet · Internet Gateway IaC Terraform ≥ 1.5 CI/CD GitHub Actions Observability Amazon CloudWatch (logs + CPU alarm)

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
Base URL (local): http://localhost:8000 Base URL (production): http://<EC2_HOST>

Interactive docs (Swagger UI): <base-url>/docs OpenAPI schema: <base-url>/openapi.json

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text:
Health check. Returns immediately with no dependencies.

Response 200 OK

{"status": "healthy"}

Example

curl http://localhost:8000/health

docs.title: GET /items
docs.text:
List all items in the store.

Response 200 OK — array of item objects (empty array if none exist)

[
  {
    "id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
    "name": "Widget",
    "description": "A sample widget",
    "price": 9.99
  }
]

Example

curl http://localhost:8000/items

docs.title: POST /items
docs.text:
Create a new item. name and price are required; description is optional.

Request body

{
  "name": "Gadget",
  "description": "Optional description",
  "price": 4.99
}

Response 201 Created

{
  "id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
  "name": "Gadget",
  "description": "Optional description",
  "price": 4.99
}

Example

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/items \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Gadget", "price": 4.99}'

docs.title: GET /items/{item_id}
docs.text:
Fetch a single item by its UUID.

Path parameter: item_id — UUID string returned by POST /items

Response 200 OK

{
  "id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
  "name": "Gadget",
  "description": null,
  "price": 4.99
}

Response 404 Not Found — if the ID does not exist

{"detail": "Item not found"}

Example

curl http://localhost:8000/items/3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6

docs.title: Data model
docs.text:
Item
├── id          string (UUID v4, assigned by server)
├── name        string (required)
├── description string | null (optional)
└── price       number (required, float)

In-memory store

Items are stored in a Python dict and are lost when the container restarts. This is intentional for the challenge scope — production would use a persistent database.

docs.title: AWS resource map
docs.text: Resource Name pattern Purpose VPC {app}-{env}-vpc Isolated network (10.0.0.0/16) Internet Gateway {app}-{env}-igw Public internet access Public subnet {app}-{env}-public-subnet EC2 host subnet (10.0.1.0/24) Route table {app}-{env}-public-rt Routes 0.0.0.0/0 → IGW Security group {app}-{env}-sg Inbound 22, 80, 443; all egress IAM role {app}-{env}-ec2-role AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly EC2 t3.micro {app}-{env} Runs the Docker container ECR repository {app}-{env} Private Docker image store CloudWatch log group /aws/ec2/{app}-{env} 7-day retention CloudWatch alarm {app}-{env}-cpu-high CPU > 80% for 4 min

docs.title: Security notes
docs.text:
• The EC2 instance has no stored AWS credentials. It authenticates to ECR via the IAM instance profile — credentials are fetched from the instance metadata service at deploy time.
  • Port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 to allow GitHub Actions runners (dynamic IPs) to SSH in. In a hardened setup this would be replaced with AWS SSM Session Manager (no port 22 at all).
  • The container listens on port 8000; the host maps it to port 80. Port 443 is open in the security group but no TLS termination is configured (see Limitations in the README).

docs.title: CI/CD Pipeline
docs.text: The pipeline lives in .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml and runs on every push to main.

docs.title: Job chain
docs.text:
push to main
     │
     ▼
build-and-test
  ├─ checkout
  ├─ pip install + pytest
  └─ docker build (smoke test)
     │ (must pass)
     ▼
push-to-ecr
  ├─ configure AWS credentials
  ├─ ecr-login
  ├─ docker build + tag (SHA + latest)
  └─ docker push both tags
     │ (must pass)
     ▼
deploy
  ├─ SSH into EC2
  ├─ aws ecr get-login-password (instance role, no stored creds)
  ├─ docker pull <SHA-tagged image>
  ├─ docker stop/rm old container
  ├─ docker run new container (-p 80:8000)
  └─ docker image prune -f

Each job needs: the previous one. A failed test blocks the push; a failed push blocks the deploy.

docs.title: Required GitHub Secrets
docs.text: Secret Used in job Purpose AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID push-to-ecr Authenticate to AWS for ECR push AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY push-to-ecr Authenticate to AWS for ECR push EC2_HOST deploy Public IP of the EC2 instance EC2_SSH_KEY deploy PEM private key for SSH login

docs.title: Image tagging strategy
docs.text:
Every push to main produces two tags:

Tag Value Purpose SHA tag abc1234... (full git SHA) Immutable reference, used for rollback latest always points to newest Convenience tag

The deploy job uses the SHA tag (passed via job output), not latest, so deployments are always deterministic.

docs.title: Job outputs wiring
docs.text:
push-to-ecr exposes two outputs consumed by deploy:

outputs:
  image:    # full ECR URI with SHA tag
  registry: # ECR registry hostname (account.dkr.ecr.region.amazonaws.com)

deploy references them as: 

${{ needs.push-to-ecr.outputs.image }}
${{ needs.push-to-ecr.outputs.registry }}

GitHub Actions resolves these before sending the SSH script to the runner — they are not shell variables.

docs.title: Manual trigger
docs.text: The workflow has workflow_dispatch: enabled, so you can trigger it manually from Actions → CI/CD Pipeline → Run workflow without pushing a commit. Useful for re-deploying after an EC2 restart.

docs.title: Updating the ECR repository name
docs.text:
ECR_REPOSITORY at the top of the workflow must match the repository Terraform created:

<app_name>-<environment>

Default values produce devops-challenge-prod. If you changed Terraform variables, update this env var to match.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• [ ] Terraform ≥ 1.5 installed (terraform -version)
  • [ ] AWS CLI installed and configured (aws configure)
  • [ ] IAM user with EC2, VPC, ECR, IAM, CloudWatch permissions
  • [ ] An existing EC2 key pair in the target region
  • [ ] GitHub repository with Actions enabled

docs.title: Step 1 — Provision infrastructure
docs.text:
cd terraform

terraform init

# Preview what will be created
terraform plan -var="key_name=<your-key-pair-name>"

# Apply (creates ~10 resources, takes ~1 min)
terraform apply -var="key_name=<your-key-pair-name>"

Note the outputs printed at the end:

ec2_public_ip      = "54.123.45.67"
ecr_repository_url = "123456789.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/devops-challenge-prod"
vpc_id             = "vpc-0abc123"

docs.title: Step 2 — Configure GitHub Secrets
docs.text:
Go to your repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret.

Secret name Value AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID IAM access key (needs ECR push + describe permissions) AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY IAM secret key EC2_HOST The ec2_public_ip from Terraform output EC2_SSH_KEY Full contents of your .pem private key file

Paste the PEM key

Open the .pem file, copy everything including the -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY----- header and footer, and paste it as the secret value.

docs.title: Step 3 — Update ECR repository name in the workflow
docs.text:
If you used non-default Terraform variable values, update ECR_REPOSITORY in .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml to match:

<app_name>-<environment>   →   devops-challenge-prod  (defaults)

docs.title: Step 4 — Trigger the pipeline
docs.text:
git add .
git commit -m "initial deployment"
git push origin main

Watch the pipeline at Actions → CI/CD Pipeline. Jobs run in order: build-and-test → push-to-ecr → deploy.

docs.title: Step 5 — Verify
docs.text:
curl http://<ec2_public_ip>/health
# {"status":"healthy"}

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
Each image is tagged with its Git SHA. To roll back to a previous version:

  1. Find the SHA of the last good commit: git log --oneline
  2. In GitHub Actions → CI/CD Pipeline → find the run with that SHA → re-run the deploy job only.

Or SSH into the instance and pull a specific tag manually:

ssh -i <key.pem> ec2-user@<EC2_HOST>
docker stop app && docker rm app
docker run -d --name app --restart unless-stopped -p 80:8000 \
  <ecr_url>:<git-sha>

docs.title: Tear down
docs.text:
cd terraform
terraform destroy -var="key_name=<your-key-pair-name>"

This removes all AWS resources created by Terraform. The ECR repository and all images will be deleted.

docs.title: Infrastructure
docs.text: All resources are managed by Terraform. No manual AWS console steps are required.

docs.title: Module structure
docs.text:
terraform/
├── main.tf          ← provider, module calls, ECR, CloudWatch
├── variables.tf     ← all input variables
├── outputs.tf       ← ec2_public_ip, ecr_repository_url, vpc_id
└── modules/
    ├── networking/  ← VPC, IGW, subnet, route table
    └── ec2/         ← instance, IAM role, security group, user_data

The root main.tf is intentionally thin — it wires the two modules together and owns resources that span both (ECR repository, CloudWatch).

docs.title: networking module
docs.text:
Inputs:

Variable Default Description app_name — Resource name prefix environment — Environment suffix vpc_cidr 10.0.0.0/16 VPC CIDR block subnet_cidr 10.0.1.0/24 Public subnet CIDR az us-east-1a Availability zone

Outputs: vpc_id, public_subnet_id

Resources created:

  • aws_vpc — DNS hostnames and support enabled
  • aws_internet_gateway — attached to the VPC
  • aws_subnet — map_public_ip_on_launch = true
  • aws_route_table — default route to IGW
  • aws_route_table_association — links subnet to route table

docs.title: ec2 module
docs.text:
Inputs:

Variable Default Description app_name — Resource name prefix environment — Environment suffix subnet_id — From networking module output vpc_id — From networking module output instance_type t3.micro EC2 instance type key_name required Existing key pair name

Outputs: instance_id, public_ip

Resources created:

  • data.aws_ami — latest Amazon Linux 2 HVM AMI (dynamically resolved)
  • aws_iam_role + aws_iam_role_policy_attachment — AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly
  • aws_iam_instance_profile — attaches role to instance
  • aws_security_group — ports 22, 80, 443 inbound; all egress
  • aws_instance — runs user_data.sh on first boot

user_data.sh installs Docker and Docker Compose on the instance so it is ready to receive deployments immediately.

docs.title: Root variables reference
docs.text: Variable Default Override with aws_region us-east-1 -var="aws_region=eu-west-1" environment prod -var="environment=staging" app_name devops-challenge -var="app_name=myapp" vpc_cidr 10.0.0.0/16 -var="vpc_cidr=172.16.0.0/16" subnet_cidr 10.0.1.0/24 -var="subnet_cidr=172.16.1.0/24" availability_zone us-east-1a -var="availability_zone=eu-west-1a" ec2_instance_type t3.micro -var="ec2_instance_type=t3.small" key_name required -var="key_name=my-key"

docs.title: CloudWatch alarm
docs.text:
The aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm resource fires when:

  • Metric: CPUUtilization on the EC2 instance
  • Threshold: > 80%
  • Evaluation: 2 periods × 2 minutes = sustained high CPU for 4 minutes

No SNS topic is wired up by default. To get notified, add an alarm_actions attribute pointing to an SNS topic ARN.

docs.title: Jenkins CI/CD Setup
docs.text: The Jenkinsfile at the project root defines the same pipeline as GitHub Actions: Checkout → Test → Build → Push to ECR → Deploy to EC2

docs.title: Start Jenkins (Docker)
docs.text:
cd jenkins
docker compose up -d

Jenkins will be available at http://localhost:8080

Get the initial admin password:

docker exec jenkins-jenkins-1 cat /var/jenkins_home/secrets/initialAdminPassword

docs.title: First-time Setup
docs.text:
1. Open http://localhost:8080 and paste the admin password
  2. Click Install suggested plugins and wait for it to finish
  3. Create your admin user
  4. Install one extra plugin: Manage Jenkins → Plugins → Available
  5. Search and install: SSH Agent Plugin
  6. Restart Jenkins after install

docs.title: Add Credentials
docs.text:
Go to Manage Jenkins → Credentials → System → Global credentials → Add Credential

Add these 5 credentials exactly as shown:

Kind ID Value Secret text AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID Your IAM access key Secret text AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Your IAM secret key Secret text ECR_REGISTRY 816880416872.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com Secret text EC2_HOST 18.212.128.34 SSH Username with private key EC2_SSH_KEY Username: ec2-user, paste contents of ~/.ssh/devops-challenge-key.pem

docs.title: Create the Pipeline
docs.text:
1. New Item → Pipeline → name it devops-challenge
  2. Under Pipeline:
  3. Definition: Pipeline script from SCM
  4. SCM: Git
  5. Repository URL: https://github.com/XKolz/devops-challenge
  6. Branch: */main
  7. Script Path: Jenkinsfile
  8. Click Save

docs.title: Run the Pipeline
docs.text:
Click Build Now. The pipeline runs through 5 stages:

Checkout → Test → Build → Push to ECR → Deploy

Watch progress under Console Output.

docs.title: Pipeline Stages Explained
docs.text: Stage What it does Checkout Clones the repo from GitHub Test Installs Python deps and runs pytest Build Builds Docker image tagged with short Git SHA Push to ECR Authenticates to ECR and pushes SHA + latest tags Deploy SSHes into EC2, pulls new image, restarts container

docs.title: Stop Jenkins
docs.text:
cd jenkins
docker compose down

Data is persisted in the jenkins_home Docker volume — your config and build history survive restarts.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker Desktop running
  • (Optional) Python 3.11 if you want to run tests without Docker

docs.title: Start the app
docs.text:
docker compose up --build

The API is live at http://localhost:8000. Interactive Swagger UI: http://localhost:8000/docs

The app/ directory is volume-mounted, so changes to Python files reload the server automatically (Uvicorn --reload is active inside the container via the volume mount).

docs.title: 2. The FastAPI Application
docs.text:
app/main.py — four endpoints, in-memory item store:

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import Optional
import uuid

app = FastAPI(title="DevOps Challenge API", version="1.0.0")

_items: dict = {}

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: Optional[str] = None
    price: float

class ItemResponse(Item):
    id: str

@app.get("/health")
def health_check():
    return {"status": "healthy"}

@app.get("/items", response_model=list[ItemResponse])
def list_items():
    return list(_items.values())

@app.get("/items/{item_id}", response_model=ItemResponse)
def get_item(item_id: str):
    if item_id not in _items:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
    return _items[item_id]

@app.post("/items", response_model=ItemResponse, status_code=201)
def create_item(item: Item):
    item_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    record = {"id": item_id, **item.model_dump()}
    _items[item_id] = record
    return record

app/requirements.txt:

fastapi==0.115.0
uvicorn[standard]==0.32.0
pydantic==2.9.2

app/Dockerfile:

FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

app/tests/test_main.py — 6 unit tests using FastAPI TestClient:

import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..")))

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app, _items

client = TestClient(app)

def setup_function():
    _items.clear()

def test_health():
    response = client.get("/health")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json() == {"status": "healthy"}

def test_list_items_empty():
    response = client.get("/items")
    assert response.json() == []

def test_create_item():
    response = client.post("/items", json={"name": "Widget", "price": 9.99})
    assert response.status_code == 201
    assert "id" in response.json()

def test_get_item():
    created = client.post("/items", json={"name": "Gadget", "price": 4.99}).json()
    response = client.get(f"/items/{created['id']}")
    assert response.status_code == 200

def test_list_items_after_create():
    client.post("/items", json={"name": "A", "price": 1.0})
    client.post("/items", json={"name": "B", "price": 2.0})
    assert len(client.get("/items").json()) == 2

def test_get_nonexistent_item():
    assert client.get("/items/does-not-exist").status_code == 404

    build: ./app

docs.title: 4. Terraform Infrastructure
docs.text: All AWS resources are managed by Terraform. The root module calls two child modules and owns ECR + CloudWatch directly.

docs.title: Provider and module wiring (terraform/main.tf)
docs.text:
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.5.0"
  required_providers {
    aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws", version = "~> 5.0" }
  }
}

provider "aws" { region = var.aws_region }

module "networking" {
  source      = "./modules/networking"
  app_name    = var.app_name
  environment = var.environment
  vpc_cidr    = var.vpc_cidr
  subnet_cidr = var.subnet_cidr
  az          = var.availability_zone
}

module "ec2" {
  source        = "./modules/ec2"
  app_name      = var.app_name
  environment   = var.environment
  subnet_id     = module.networking.public_subnet_id
  vpc_id        = module.networking.vpc_id
  instance_type = var.ec2_instance_type
  key_name      = var.key_name
}

resource "aws_ecr_repository" "app" {
  name                 = "${var.app_name}-${var.environment}"
  image_tag_mutability = "MUTABLE"
  image_scanning_configuration { scan_on_push = true }
}

resource "aws_cloudwatch_log_group" "app" {
  name              = "/aws/ec2/${var.app_name}-${var.environment}"
  retention_in_days = 7
}

resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm" "cpu_high" {
  alarm_name          = "${var.app_name}-${var.environment}-cpu-high"
  comparison_operator = "GreaterThanThreshold"
  evaluation_periods  = 2
  metric_name         = "CPUUtilization"
  namespace           = "AWS/EC2"
  period              = 120
  statistic           = "Average"
  threshold           = 80
  dimensions          = { InstanceId = module.ec2.instance_id }
}

docs.title: Networking module (terraform/modules/networking/main.tf)
docs.text:
Creates: VPC → Internet Gateway → Public Subnet → Route Table → Association

resource "aws_vpc" "main" {
  cidr_block           = var.vpc_cidr
  enable_dns_hostnames = true
  enable_dns_support   = true
}

resource "aws_internet_gateway" "main" { vpc_id = aws_vpc.main.id }

resource "aws_subnet" "public" {
  vpc_id                  = aws_vpc.main.id
  cidr_block              = var.subnet_cidr
  availability_zone       = var.az
  map_public_ip_on_launch = true
}

resource "aws_route_table" "public" {
  vpc_id = aws_vpc.main.id
  route { cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0"; gateway_id = aws_internet_gateway.main.id }
}

resource "aws_route_table_association" "public" {
  subnet_id      = aws_subnet.public.id
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.public.id
}

docs.title: EC2 module (terraform/modules/ec2/main.tf)
docs.text:
Creates: IAM role + profile → Security group → EC2 instance

data "aws_ami" "amazon_linux_2" {
  most_recent = true
  owners      = ["amazon"]
  filter { name = "name"; values = ["amzn2-ami-hvm-*-x86_64-gp2"] }
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "ec2" {
  name               = "${var.app_name}-${var.environment}-ec2-role"
  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{ Action = "sts:AssumeRole", Effect = "Allow",
      Principal = { Service = "ec2.amazonaws.com" } }]
  })
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "ecr_read" {
  role       = aws_iam_role.ec2.name
  policy_arn = "arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly"
}

resource "aws_iam_instance_profile" "ec2" {
  name = "${var.app_name}-${var.environment}-ec2-profile"
  role = aws_iam_role.ec2.name
}

resource "aws_security_group" "app" {
  vpc_id = var.vpc_id
  ingress { from_port = 22;  to_port = 22;  protocol = "tcp"; cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"] }
  ingress { from_port = 80;  to_port = 80;  protocol = "tcp"; cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"] }
  ingress { from_port = 443; to_port = 443; protocol = "tcp"; cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"] }
  egress  { from_port = 0;   to_port = 0;   protocol = "-1";  cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"] }
}

resource "aws_instance" "app" {
  ami                    = data.aws_ami.amazon_linux_2.id
  instance_type          = var.instance_type
  subnet_id              = var.subnet_id
  key_name               = var.key_name
  iam_instance_profile   = aws_iam_instance_profile.ec2.name
  vpc_security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.app.id]
  user_data              = base64encode(file("${path.module}/user_data.sh"))
}

docs.title: 7. GitHub Actions CI/CD
docs.text:
.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml — triggers on push to main, runs 3 sequential jobs:

build-and-test → push-to-ecr → deploy
  • build-and-test: installs deps, runs pytest, builds Docker image as smoke test
  • push-to-ecr: authenticates to ECR, pushes image tagged with Git SHA + latest
  • deploy: SSHes into EC2, authenticates via IAM instance role, pulls and restarts container

docs.title: Create pipeline
docs.text:
New Item → Pipeline → devops-challenge

Under Pipeline section: - Definition: Pipeline script from SCM - SCM: Git - Repository URL: https://github.com/XKolz/devops-challenge - Branch: */main - Script Path: Jenkinsfile

docs.title: Jenkinsfile — pipeline stages
docs.text:
pipeline {
    agent any
    environment {
        AWS_REGION     = 'us-east-1'
        ECR_REPOSITORY = 'devops-challenge-prod'
    }
    stages {
        stage('Checkout') { steps { checkout scm } }

        stage('Test') {
            steps {
                sh '''
                    python3 -m venv /tmp/test-venv
                    /tmp/test-venv/bin/pip install --quiet -r app/requirements.txt pytest httpx
                    /tmp/test-venv/bin/pytest app/tests/ -v
                '''
            }
        }

        stage('Build') {
            steps {
                script { env.IMAGE_TAG = sh(script: 'git rev-parse --short HEAD', returnStdout: true).trim() }
                sh 'docker build -t ${ECR_REPOSITORY}:${IMAGE_TAG} ./app'
            }
        }

        stage('Push to ECR') {
            steps {
                withCredentials([
                    string(credentialsId: 'AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID',     variable: 'AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID'),
                    string(credentialsId: 'AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY', variable: 'AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY'),
                    string(credentialsId: 'ECR_REGISTRY',          variable: 'ECR_REGISTRY')
                ]) {
                    sh '''
                        export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
                        export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
                        export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=$AWS_REGION
                        aws ecr get-login-password --region $AWS_REGION \
                          | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin $ECR_REGISTRY
                        docker tag  ${ECR_REPOSITORY}:${IMAGE_TAG} $ECR_REGISTRY/${ECR_REPOSITORY}:${IMAGE_TAG}
                        docker tag  ${ECR_REPOSITORY}:${IMAGE_TAG} $ECR_REGISTRY/${ECR_REPOSITORY}:latest
                        docker push $ECR_REGISTRY/${ECR_REPOSITORY}:${IMAGE_TAG}
                        docker push $ECR_REGISTRY/${ECR_REPOSITORY}:latest
                    '''
                }
            }
        }

        stage('Deploy') {
            steps {
                withCredentials([
                    string(credentialsId: 'ECR_REGISTRY', variable: 'ECR_REGISTRY'),
                    string(credentialsId: 'EC2_HOST',     variable: 'EC2_HOST'),
                    sshUserPrivateKey(credentialsId: 'EC2_SSH_KEY', keyFileVariable: 'SSH_KEY_FILE')
                ]) {
                    sh '''
                        ssh -i "$SSH_KEY_FILE" -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no ec2-user@"$EC2_HOST" "
                          aws ecr get-login-password --region $AWS_REGION \
                            | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin $ECR_REGISTRY
                          docker pull $ECR_REGISTRY/$ECR_REPOSITORY:$IMAGE_TAG
                          docker stop app 2>/dev/null || true
                          docker rm   app 2>/dev/null || true
                          docker run -d --name app --restart unless-stopped \
                            -p 80:8000 $ECR_REGISTRY/$ECR_REPOSITORY:$IMAGE_TAG
                          docker image prune -f
                        "
                    '''
                }
            }
        }
    }
    post {
        success { echo 'Pipeline completed successfully — app is live.' }
        failure { echo 'Pipeline failed. Check the stage logs above.' }
    }
}

docs.title: 11. Tear Down
docs.text:
To destroy all AWS resources:

cd terraform
terraform destroy -var="key_name=devops-challenge-key"

To also remove the key pair:

aws ec2 delete-key-pair --key-name devops-challenge-key
rm ~/.ssh/devops-challenge-key.pem

To stop Jenkins:

cd jenkins
docker compose down
